scenes.tts: Capsaicin, the molecule in chili peppers, carries no heat. So why does it burn?
scenes.visual: A red chili pepper beside a thermometer that reads skin temperature, unchanged. The question appears on screen.
scenes.narration: Capsaicin, the molecule in chili peppers, carries no heat. So why does it burn?

scenes.tts: Caterina, Julius and colleagues looked for the protein that capsaicin acts on.
scenes.visual: Names on screen: Caterina, Julius and colleagues, 1997. A sensory neuron with a question mark on its membrane.
scenes.narration: Caterina, Julius and colleagues looked for the protein that capsaicin acts on.

scenes.tts: They used cells that do not normally respond to capsaicin.
scenes.visual: A dish of cells labelled HEK293 cells: no response to capsaicin.
scenes.narration: They used cells that do not normally respond to capsaicin.

scenes.tts: They added pools of C D N A, copies of sensory neuron genes, and watched calcium inside the cells.
scenes.caption: They added pools of cDNA, copies of sensory neuron genes, and watched calcium inside the cells.
scenes.visual: Pools of cDNA from rodent dorsal root ganglia drop into dishes. Beside each dish, a calcium trace against time.
scenes.narration: They added pools of cDNA, copies of sensory neuron genes, and watched calcium inside the cells.

scenes.tts: With most pools, capsaicin did nothing.
scenes.visual: Capsaicin arrives (marked on the time axis); most traces stay flat.
scenes.narration: With most pools, capsaicin did nothing.

scenes.tts: A positive pool made the trace jump. Splitting that pool again and again left a single C D N A.
scenes.caption: A positive pool made the trace jump. Splitting that pool again and again left a single cDNA.
scenes.visual: One trace jumps at the capsaicin mark. The positive pool splits into smaller pools, down to one cDNA.
scenes.narration: A positive pool made the trace jump. Splitting that pool again and again left a single cDNA.

scenes.tts: It made a channel now called T R P V one.
scenes.caption: It made a channel now called TRPV1.
scenes.visual: Label: VR1, now called TRPV1, a nonselective cation channel.
scenes.narration: It made a channel now called TRPV1.

scenes.tts: Here is the surprise. The same channel also opens with heat above about forty-three degrees.
scenes.caption: Here is the surprise. The same channel also opens with heat above about 43 °C.
scenes.visual: A temperature readout climbs past 43 °C and the same trace jumps again. Small note: cloned rat channel, in a foreign cell.
scenes.narration: Here is the surprise. The same channel also opens with heat above about 43 °C.

scenes.tts: That was the cloned rat channel, in a foreign cell, not human perception.
scenes.visual: The note enlarges: cloned rat channel, heterologous cells, not human perception.
scenes.narration: That was the cloned rat channel, in a foreign cell, not human perception.

scenes.tts: So capsaicin burns without heat. It excites sensory neurons that noxious heat also excites.
scenes.visual: Capsaicin and a flame icon both open TRPV1 in the same sensory neuron. One output arrow: activity in heat-sensitive neurons.
scenes.narration: So capsaicin burns without heat. It excites sensory neurons that noxious heat also excites.

scenes.tts: Predict. A chemical opens a channel that cool temperatures also open. How will it feel on the skin?
scenes.visual: A blank channel with a snowflake icon and a chemical icon both pointing at it. The question on screen.
scenes.narration: Predict. A chemical opens a channel that cool temperatures also open. How will it feel on the skin?

scenes.tts: Most likely cool, if it mainly drives cold-sensitive neurons. That chemical is menthol. Mint can feel cool without the skin cooling.
scenes.visual: A mint leaf. The thermometer stays put while the label reads: a cooling feeling need not mean cooler skin.
scenes.narration: Most likely cool, if it mainly drives cold-sensitive neurons. That chemical is menthol. Mint can feel cool without the skin cooling.

scenes.tts: Its receptor is called T R P M eight. Cool temperatures open it too.
scenes.caption: Its receptor is called TRPM8. Cool temperatures open it too.
scenes.visual: Label: TRPM8, opened by menthol and by cool-to-cold temperatures (McKemy and colleagues, 2002).
scenes.narration: Its receptor is called TRPM8. Cool temperatures open it too.

scenes.tts: But cloning shows only what is enough in a foreign cell. Does the animal need it?
scenes.visual: Two words on screen: sufficient (foreign cell) and necessary (animal), with a question mark over the second.
scenes.narration: But cloning shows only what is enough in a foreign cell. Does the animal need it?

scenes.tts: Back to T R P V one. Caterina and colleagues knocked that gene out in mice.
scenes.caption: Back to TRPV1. Caterina and colleagues knocked that gene out in mice.
scenes.visual: A mouse labelled VR1-null (TRPV1 knockout) beside a littermate control. Caterina and colleagues, 2000.
scenes.narration: Back to TRPV1. Caterina and colleagues knocked that gene out in mice.

scenes.tts: The mice showed no pain behaviour to capsaicin. Their detection of painful heat was only partly impaired.
scenes.visual: Result rows: capsaicin response, gone; hot plate, partly impaired.
scenes.narration: The mice showed no pain behaviour to capsaicin. Their detection of painful heat was only partly impaired.

scenes.tts: Mechanical responses were normal, and the heat loss was partial. So other sensors exist, and T R P V one is not the pain receptor.
scenes.caption: Mechanical responses were normal, and the heat loss was partial. So other sensors exist, and TRPV1 is not the pain receptor.
scenes.visual: Third row: filament poke, normal. Caption: heat loss partial, mechanical normal; other sensors exist; TRPV1 is not the pain receptor.
scenes.narration: Mechanical responses were normal, and the heat loss was partial. So other sensors exist, and TRPV1 is not the pain receptor.

scenes.tts: That gives the lesson its one idea. Follow the line.
scenes.visual: Guiding-idea card titled Follow the line, with three slots: report, route, volume. Only the first will fill in this film.
scenes.narration: That gives the lesson its one idea. Follow the line.

scenes.tts: A sensory neuron's firing says which line is active, and how strongly. But it does not say for certain what activated it.
scenes.visual: Slot one fills: report. Firing identifies the active line; it need not uniquely identify what activated it.
scenes.narration: A sensory neuron's firing says which line is active, and how strongly. But it does not say for certain what activated it.

scenes.tts: The channels in its endings decide what can activate it.
scenes.visual: Capsaicin, heat and protons all point at TRPV1 in one ending; a snowflake and menthol point at TRPM8 in another.
scenes.narration: The channels in its endings decide what can activate it.

scenes.tts: The next two films follow where each line goes, and who turns it up.
scenes.visual: Slots two and three, route and volume, glow with the labels: next films.
scenes.narration: The next two films follow where each line goes, and who turns it up.

scenes.tts: So when something burns, ask first. Which neurons were driven, and what can drive them?
scenes.visual: Takeaway card: firing identifies the active line; it need not uniquely identify what activated it.
scenes.narration: So when something burns, ask first. Which neurons were driven, and what can drive them?
